source: TSTD/MAFF Pumpkin (ល្ពៅ) Cultivation Manual, PDF title "10_Pumpkin_manual_body+covers" (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), 2012
text: Pumpkin seedlings are transplanted from the nursery into the field at roughly 7-12 days old, once the true leaves have emerged, ideally in the cooler part of the day (early morning or late afternoon) to reduce transplant shock. Before transplanting, planting holes in the field should already be dug, filled with a mix of soil and well-decomposed organic matter, and watered so the soil is moist. The seedling and its surrounding growing medium (from the nursery bag or tray) are placed into the hole together to minimize root disturbance, then firmed in place with surrounding soil. Watering after transplanting is important to help roots establish.
caveat: The precise seedling age window (7-12 days) is reconstructed from partially garbled numerals in the source and should be verified against a clean scan before treating it as an exact figure.
